review_log_2026_10_03.scope: public-source recheck for an untouched independent full-loop HRS validation set

sources_checked.finding: official field report; no machine-readable synchronized raw trace or embedded attachment
public accepted manuscript; describes one-year station data but no downloadable synchronized raw trace
validated software and empirical-data description; download is registration-gated and no raw independent archive exposed
official statement that partner raw data are secured; only aggregate CDPs are public
peer-reviewed four-year 3Emotion HRS/bus operational analysis; reports aggregate fill mass and duration but no synchronized raw trace
public report describes 18 GasTeF recorded-data files, but the files and reuse terms are not exposed by the public resource
NREL HITRF 36 L fill is described with 6.3 to 73.0 MPa and 186 s boundaries, but the paper states that research data are not shared

CC BY 4.0 Zenodo record exposes three XLSX time series from HySaM hydrogen sampling-system experiments; raw files have pressure/temperature/flow-like channels but no vehicle/tank/refuelling context, so they cannot close the HRS full-loop gate.

2026 BAM demonstration-HRS paper reports eight field safety sensors and three days of chronological monitoring, but its data-availability statement provides no raw download and directs requests to the corresponding author; no vehicle-side full-loop archive is exposed.

CEC HyStEP report documents 11 station campaigns with three instrumented Type IV 70 MPa tanks, protocol/fault/communication tests and pressure/temperature/fueling measurements; it explicitly states station test data and results are confidential and not included, so retain as a data-request lead only.

Real-station 35/70 MPa fill study exposes four CSV downloads containing only initial/final summary tables; reported pressure/temperature/flow plots lack a downloadable common-time-base trace, so retain as a summary benchmark and raw-trace request lead.

Open paper prints a 24-channel HRS sensor schema and 1 s normal-operation examples, but vehicle-side pressure/mass-flow channels are absent and abnormal component values were artificially created; retain as a sensor-schema benchmark only.

NIST field-test standard reports seven H2 drafts at a retail dispenser with continuous tank pressure/temperature and independent mass methods (field agreement within 1.53%), but no machine-readable synchronized logger files are public and dispenser readout was disabled; retain as a raw-trace metrology request lead.

Official CC BY 4.0 export API exposes station layout plus availability, usage, derived low-storage status, pricing, events and photos; it does not expose synchronized pressure/temperature/flow or numeric inventory traces, so it is operations context only.

The open IJHE paper reports real FCH2RAIL HRS/train measurements and 32 days of refuelling analysis, but explicitly says rail-vehicle refuelling measurement data were not publicly available; the DLR record and Crossref metadata expose no synchronized machine-readable archive or supplementary dataset.

Official H2FillS package contains a 351-row, 1 s, 7-tank Type IV HDVS physical sample workbook. Frozen tank-submodel screening gives 0/7 joint passes (mean pressure RMSE 6.164 MPa; temperature RMSE 4.625 C); package licence blocks redistribution and the workbook lacks station-side full-loop channels.

review_log_2026_10_03.result: H2Protocol raw archives remain consumed Powertech evidence. The NREL H2FillS package adds an independent physical HDVS tank-submodel candidate with a reproducible negative screen and an EOS-implied-volume mismatch diagnostic, but its licence and missing station-side channels prevent a full-loop claim. DOE/NREL aggregate reporting also identifies a second October 2022 HDVS campaign; without synchronized raw traces it remains operating-range context only.
